paraphrase: Vācaspati salutes Śiva — all-pervading, all-powerful, bearer of the bow Pināka, maker, knower and destroyer of the universe — and Akṣapāda, rich in dharma, knowledge, dispassion and lordship; he wishes to earn some merit by rescuing the very old cows of Uddyotakara (his words), sunk in the mire of hard-to-cross bad commentaries. He explains that Uddyotakara wrote because the śāstra, though explained by Pakṣilasvāmin, had been obscured by later bad reasoners such as Dignāga.
